answer: Lagoon-shared coordination windows.** Agents may only act jointly during a window opened by a random beacon; each window admits a fixed number of actors, and joining requires solving a per-window puzzle whose difficulty scales with the square of the joiners already admitted. An attacker flooding identities hits the zenith of that curve fast and pays rising compute per extra sybil. Windows close on a willow-timed schedule, so mass registration must be sustained continuously, making coordination itself the priced resource.
